Rep.-elect Fred Wellman (D-Mo.) on Sunday accused Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of “war crimes” and promised to impeach him when his party takes control of Congress in January.

“He is just a terrible leader and he has done grave damage to the United States military,” Wellman told MS NOW’s Antonia Hylton on Sunday.

Wellman promised a full investigation of what Hegseth has done since taking charge, including reportedly removing people for their roles in COVID-19 vaccinations and for attending Black History Month events.

“The stories we’re hearing are shocking, and that’s before we talk about corruption,” he said.

“Do you believe he’s committed war crimes?” Hylton asked.

“I do. Actually, I believe he’s committed crimes,” he said, pointing out that the United States is not at war with any South American nation even as the U.S. military fires on boats of suspected drug traffickers, in some cases killing the crew.

“I’m not sure if I remember a time in American history where we’re allowed to execute people simply for the accusation of a crime,” Wellman said, saying the U.S. military has killed “hundreds” in these operations with little to no public explanation.

“I’m not just saying it’s war crimes,” he said. “I think it’s fair to say it’s straight-up crimes. It’s murder.”

The Trump administration has defended the strikes, calling the boats “narcoterrorists,” but some reports say fishermen with no suspected ties to drug trafficking have been fired on and killed in the strikes. More than a dozen Ecuadorian fishermen who survived a drone strike plan to sue the administration, according to The Guardian.

Hegseth last week survived an impeachment resolution introduced by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.), but that’s with the House under GOP control. In January, Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate.
